tasks.summary: Built S1.tooling in the pipeline repo. It adds rules.schema.json (format_version 1, kind area and merged, spec_version ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$, lookups[].values only with copy_values true, additionalProperties false at every level). It adds data-model.schema.json, which reuses the table and relationship shapes from model.schema.json by $ref through a referencing registry. Shared logic is in toolkit/rules.py, with five subcommands: rules-lint, rules-coverage, rules-render, spec-check and schema-lint. They exit 0 on a pass, 1 when a check fails and 2 when an input is missing, and they follow the MP_QUIET=1 summary contract. Every problem names its JSON pointer. The synthetic fixtures describe an invented book-lending Access app and an invented fines-ledger workbook. 76 tests pass, including the S1.areas and S5.features items_from jq programs run with jq 1.8.1 on valid.json, and a check that both programs match the copies in docs/contracts.md#rules-json. All 11 acceptance commands pass, the guard included.
notes: Every fixture is invented (book-lending Access app 'booklend-demo', fines-ledger workbook 'booklend-ledger'). None contains Northwind or InvoiceGenerator names or text. The invalid-*.json variants, analysis/rules.json, gates.json and the change orders came from throwaway scripts in the session scratchpad and are not committed. analysis/rules.json is valid.json with spec_version 1.1. gates.json S1 holds the hashes of valid.json and of a 1.0 rules.md. CO-001 is approved with the current hashes, and CO-002 is pending on top of CO-001.

Design choice: rules-lint runs the semantic checks only once the file passes the jsonschema, so a malformed file reports schema pointers first. rules-coverage and rules-render also require schema validity and exit 1 with 'run rules-lint' otherwise.

Checks added beyond the spec list: an objects[], services[] or open_questions[] id must name an existing area. workflows[].id and services[].name must be unique. In a kind area file, services must also belong to the area.
Assumption: rules-render --check exits 1 when keep-drop.md is missing, following the Conventions rule that a missing output counts as a difference. A missing rules file exits 2.

Assumption: spec-check picks the pending change order as the highest-numbered CO-NNN.md that both has no approved gates.json entry and has base_rules_sha256 equal to the approved rules hash. A gates.json CO entry with an empty approved field does not count as approved.

The rule trigger pattern in rules.schema.json encodes the trigger forms from contracts.md#rules-json: form:, report:, datamacro:, macro:, procedure:, query:, cell:<Sheet>!<A1>, and schedule:startup|timer:|ontime:|task:. A kept object's target_component must be <area>.<module>, legacy.models or foundation:<what>.

issues.problem: The original's 'Add Reorder Items' action works in every saved status, but no rule says so or decides what the new app should do. It conflicts with R-purchasing-012, which freezes lines from Submitted on. R-purchasing-021 says only 'on a saved purchase order'. In the original, the action adds lines to Submitted, Approved, Received and even Closed purchase orders. On an Approved one, that raises the on-order figure. Either restrict R-021 to New purchase orders (a stated change) or raise a client question. The merged rules.json carries the same pair of rules unchanged.
issues.evidence: In out/model/code/Form_frmPurchaseOrderDetails.txt, cmdAddNostock_Click (lines 104-135) refuses only a new record and otherwise runs a direct insert into PurchaseOrderDetails, with no status check. LockControls (lines 475-531) never lists cmdAddNostock. In objects.json, the frmPurchaseOrderDetails control cmdAddNostock is a visible CommandButton in FormHeader. Form_Current (lines 395-401) restricts only the subform's AllowAdditions/Edits/Deletions to New. rules.json: R-purchasing-012 says 'from Submitted on the lines are frozen'; R-purchasing-021 says 'On a saved purchase order, one action adds a line...'.

issues.problem: R-orders-049 contradicts R-orders-031 on the audit date columns. R-049 says the first-run job moves every date in every table forward and that the rows it changes are stamped System under R-orders-031. R-031 says an update keeps the original created-on even when the update tries to change it, and sets modified-on to now. Applied together, created-on is not shifted and modified-on is overwritten with the current time instead of being shifted. In the original, the shift runs before the audit data macros are installed (the shift procedure runs first, then the installer). The spec should say what happens to the created-by/on and modified-by/on columns during the shift.
issues.evidence: In out/model/code/modGlobal.txt, OneTimeProcessing (lines 255-283) calls SetDatesToCurrent before AddDataMacros. In modOrders.txt, SetDatesToCurrent (lines 190-227) updates every date field in every non-system table. In modTableDataMacros.txt, AddDataMacros adds the audit macros 'if they don't exist'. In datamacros.json, Orders.BeforeChange restores the old AddedOn on update. rules.json: R-orders-049 says 'moves every date in every table forward' and 'rows it changes are stamped with the name System (R-orders-031)'. R-orders-031 says it 'keeps the original created-by and created-on even if an update tries to change or blank them'. rules.md line 370 repeats that the date shift is a system job stamped System.

issues.problem: R-purchasing-014 leaves out that deleting a purchase order asks for confirmation. The original deletes through the standard delete-record command.
